The leaves of a depth-$\mathrm{D}$ decision tree partition $\mathrm{Dom}(f)$
into subcubes of codimension at most $\mathrm{D}$, each monochromatic. So the
subcube-partition model is at least as strong as the decision-tree model, and
the interesting question is by how much -- see the reverse pair.

every coordinate is fixed.

facts: $\mathrm{D}(f) = O(\mathrm{SP}(f)^2)$, and this is essentially tight: [AKK16] give a total $f$ with $\mathrm{D}(f) = \tilde\Omega(\mathrm{SP}(f)^2)$, in fact already $\mathrm{R}(f) = \tilde\Omega(\mathrm{SP}(f)^2)$. The first separation of any kind is [KRS15]; the power-$1.5$ stage is the query half of [GPW18].

Quantum is not settled: $\mathrm{Q} = \tilde\Omega(\mathrm{SP}^{1.5})$ [AKK16] against the $O(\mathrm{SP}^2)$ ceiling. The quadratic quantum separation in [AKK16], like the $\log^2\chi_1$ bound of [GPW18], is against the one-sided partition number -- a different measure, and not one the zoo carries.
